name: comp-266
title: Audio Equalizer Slider
description: A graphic equalizer: five vertical sliders spaced evenly under the heading Equalizer, each capped with a white pill handle and named by a frequency underneath.
use: A player or mixer needs a compact multi-band tone control with visible band names.
avoid: Bands, their defaults and the minus five to five range are fixed in the source with no props.
a11y: Each fader has a frequency name and arrow keys work, but the heading uses a legend outside any fieldset so the group is loose. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: The word Equalizer heads a row of five upright tracks. Each track has a white pill-shaped handle at a different height, with a bright white length beneath it, and a small grey frequency label sits under every track.
behaves: Each handle slides up or down its own track between minus five and five and carries a soft ring while held; a small value tip is set to appear during use. The other four faders stay put.
customise: Band labels, starting levels, the heading and the value range are all written in the source; adding a band means copying a block.
weight: light: Five small vertical sliders; nothing animates unless a handle is moved.
demo: Five bands labelled 60, 250, 1k, 4k and 16K, opening at raised, slight boost, flat and cut positions.
issues: No zero line or scale, so it is hard to tell a cut band from a boosted one.
The heading is a legend element with no surrounding fieldset.
polishWhy: Even, quiet faders that read as an EQ, but with no scale marks for reference.
